quiz.q: What is the default level of the Logger component?
quiz.explain: The Logger prints at INFO by default; its dropdown has DEBUG, ERROR, INFO, TRACE, WARN — FATAL isn't there.

quiz.q: What is the order of log levels from least to most severe?
options: DEBUG < TRACE < INFO < ERROR < WARN < FATAL
TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR < FATAL
INFO < DEBUG < TRACE < WARN < ERROR < FATAL
FATAL < ERROR < WARN < INFO < DEBUG < TRACE
quiz.explain: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR < FATAL.

quiz.q: An app's logging level is set to INFO. Which levels are printed?
quiz.explain: A selected level prints itself and everything more severe.

quiz.q: A request fails in production and info/error logs don't show why. Which level do you usually enable?
quiz.explain: In real time DEBUG is usually enabled for such cases; TRACE is more in-depth and rarely needed.

quiz.q: In Runtime Manager → Settings → Logging, you set DEBUG for package `org.mule`. What gets debug logs?
options: The whole application — listener, logger, transforms and all connectors
quiz.explain: `org.mule` covers the whole app; a connector's own package (e.g. `org.mule.extension.http`) limits it to that connector.

quiz.q: Why shouldn't verbose logging stay on?
options: It prints a lot and slows the app, causing performance issues
It is not supported on CloudHub
quiz.explain: Enable it briefly, for one connector's package, only when you can't find or replicate the issue — then disable it.
`flatten` removes the first level of inner arrays and merges their values into the main array.

quiz.q: `arr flatMap $.empId` failed with "Expecting type Array". Why?
options: The flatMap mapper must return an array for each item, but it returned a single value
quiz.explain: flatMap = map + flatten; per its signature the mapper returns `Array<R>`.

quiz.q: How do you declare a custom (named) function in DataWeave?
options: `function add(n, m) { n + m }` in the body
`fun add(n, m) = n + m` in the header
quiz.explain: Use the `fun` keyword in the header, then call `add(1, 2)` in the body.

quiz.q: Inside `payload.bookstore.*book map ((item, index) -> …)`, how do you get each book's own `category` attribute?
quiz.explain: `payload.bookstore.book.@category` gives only the first book's value ("cooking" for all); `item.@category` reads each one.

quiz.q: JSON → XML fails with "Trying to output second root, bookstore, while writing Xml". What's the rule?
options: XML allows only one root element — wrap the output in a single-key object, e.g. `{ bookstore: { book: payload } }`
quiz.explain: XML can have only one root element, given as a key–value inside an object.

quiz.q: How do you remove the header row from CSV output?
quiz.explain: By default the header row (the keys) is included; `header=false` removes it.

cards.back: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR < FATAL. A selected level prints itself and everything more severe.
**INFO**. FATAL isn't in the Logger dropdown.
Prints only when there is an error. Choose INFO to print every time.
Potentially harmful situations; mostly ignored because they don't affect the process.
DEBUG gives detailed component/connector info when info/error logs aren't enough; TRACE is even deeper, uses more space, and is used very rarely.

cards.front: How do you get more detail for a production issue on CloudHub?
cards.back: Runtime Manager → app → Settings → Logging → DEBUG for a package (the connector's, not `org.mule`) → Apply Changes, reproduce, then turn it off.
`org.mule` = debug logs for the whole app; `org.mule.extension.http` = only HTTP listener and request.

cards.front: Where do you find a connector's package name?
cards.back: Open that connector's configuration and copy its package name.
Detailed logging — slows the app. Enable briefly, for one connector's package, and disable right after.
The app's logging configuration file.
Removes **one** level of nested arrays: `flatten([1,2,3,[4,5],[8]])` → `[1,2,3,4,5,8]`.

cards.front: `flatten(a + b)` with two arrays of employees
cards.back: `a + b` adds b as one inner array; `flatten` removes it, giving one array of all employee objects.
`flatten` removes one level of nesting. `flatMap` maps each item and flattens in one step; its mapper must return an array.
Declared in the header: `fun add(n, m) = n + m`; call `add(1, 2)` → 3.
The single top-level tag (e.g. `bookstore`) holding everything. XML allows only one.
Metadata in the opening tag, value in double quotes — e.g. `category="cooking"`.
Elements at the same level under one parent — book 1, book 2, book 3.
Returns all repeated elements as an array — `payload.bookstore.*book`.

cards.front: How do you read an XML attribute?
cards.back: With `@` — `item.@category` inside a map over `*book`.
Elements come through, but attributes (like `category`) don't.

cards.front: Why does JSON → XML fail with "second root"?
cards.back: Only one root element is allowed. Wrap the output: `{ bookstore: { book: payload } }`.

cards.front: How do you write an attribute when producing XML?
cards.back: `name @(lastName: person.LastName, age: person.Age): person.name`

cards.front: How do you drop the header row in CSV output?
cards.back: `output application/csv header=false`.
